hook: SCP-030 is a small grey clay person who is awake only while light falls on it and goes inert in the dark. There's no horror here; the containment file reads more like the terms of a cautious scholarly arrangement than a cell. The tension comes from deciding what this polite, curious being should be allowed to learn.
whyItMatters: 030 sits in the gentle, sapient corner of the series: an anomaly kept close because its mind is useful, and risky only in quiet, hypothetical ways. Most of its procedures are paperwork, from written consultations to thirty days' notice for meetings in person and a supervised outing of one hour at most, and that bureaucracy shows how the Foundation handles a valued, harmless mind. The suspected link to the Alchemists of Alagadda is offered only as a suspicion based on its makeup and where it was found.
thingsToNotice: Look at what is restricted: no modern science journals, and no fiction newer than 1623, explicitly to keep its "innate knowledge" uncontaminated. Its body is mostly clay from around London, with mandrake, lye, mercury and human blood turning up in every sample, and it was found in an unmarked infant-sized stone coffin in Mortlake, politely wishing the construction crew a good afternoon the moment sunlight reached it. The one rote answer it gives about its maker, that it was asked to forget, is the article's single locked door. The addendum log escalates quietly: it offers to repair its own tracker, teaches an unknown language to five researchers, overhears a stray remark about photovoltaics, asks for magnesium to burn, and finally builds an ultraviolet emitter out of potting soil, ginger, rutilated quartz and copper wire. The file ends with all of its research suspended while the Foundation decides whether a creature that runs on light should keep studying light.
